What can you do to improve your focus/productivity?

Break everything down into small easily accomplishable tasks and then mix them up. This way it's not too boring and you'll get the rewarding feeling of getting something done often. You don't want to face one huge task, that's demotivating and you'll likely procrastinate. Sort the tasks from not-too-bad, to bad, to easy. Don't start with the worst, or you'll probably never start and don't move the worst to the end, or you might give up before it.

Here is an example. If your tasks for today are to clean your entire apartment, shop groceries and bring the trash out, don't just try to do one thing after another. Cleaning your apartment is a big task that needs to be broken down. Also you don't want to be cleaning for hours, so mix it with the other tasks. A possible order could be: clean kitchen (not too bad), bring trash out, clean bathroom (bad), shop groceries (nice distraction from cleaning), clean bedroom (easy). But that depends entirely on your preferences.

You might add something rewarding in the middle, e.g. after completing half or the worst of the tasks, browse a half an hour on voat. But be careful to limit this strictly or you won't start again. So don't do this until the worst is already done and you might as well finish the rest.

For me personally, as an alternative perspective, there is very little "thinking work" that I would perform better with music as compared to low level white noise or subtle nature sounds. Music would only improve my work if it was an alternative to listing to people around me talk or some other more distracting noise. Music could on the other hand help me for any activity that was very routine and didn't require critical thinking.

Genre matters on the task at hand. I've heard Reggae is the best to listen to while studying or doing desk work because it "has the rhythm of the heart". If you're working out or doing manual labor Rock or any other fast/heavy style can help.

1. Keep a time journal. Record everything you do no matter how trivial and after a couple of weeks you'll have a good picture of how you're REALLY spending your time.

  2. Make a priority list of what is important to you//what you want to accomplish.

  3. Remove everything from #1 that doesn't support #2.

  4. Repeat monthly, everyone slips.

  5. Set an alarm and start getting up on time. The snooze button is for losers.
